18.transcript:
Caleb never showed me just a finished piece. I stood right behind him, over his shoulder, watching his mistakes—those times where he got it so wrong and became very frustrated. I was making fixes in my head. He had a way of explaining why every decision was made. He is a master of the craft. First it was Microsoft Paint, then Photoshop , and now physical media. I saw him go through countless iterations just to get one single image right. It was never about the tools. It was the psychology behind those countless iterations. Try a little, then try again. That is what I want to pass on. The understanding of why the tool is built this way and not any other way. Because there was no blueprint. 

The tool should only facilitate mastery. Understanding why the tool is built this way will help the next person take after me. I don't have to say medicine is a tool—it is a tool. But there is human consciousness, which is far bigger. Once a human being is able to understand something to the nth degree, a solution naturally emerges that is even bigger than whatever had already been thought about. 

I learned this through training under a master craftsman, which inspired me to create immersive education that mentors you in real time as you watch. It helps you become a master physician regardless of your prior education. The goal is to achieve mastery so that those who follow won’t have to rely on memorization. Why memorize when students can strive for true understanding instead?
